notes: This part is NOT finished. The session's web search allowance was already spent (the first search went through, the next six were refused), so pages were read directly with the kit's honest User-Agent (states/net.py), one request at a time, robots.txt read first for each site (and a site was left alone if its robots.txt turns away the kit's name or any of Anthropic's named agents). After the campaign websites filed with the Secretary of State and the party pages had been read, the session's permission system refused the next batch of requests: the thirteen county and city governments' own pages for the county and city candidates. Nothing was done to get around that refusal and no further pages were asked for, so the following have no findings because they were never researched, not because nothing exists: Matt Kelm, Danny O'Keefe, Robert Preble, Jennae Hoffman, James Kunze, Michelle Duncan, Mark Ellerbusch, Rachel V. Cornelius, Najwa Massad, Wayne B. Erickson, Aaron G. Stritesky, Jerome Christenson, Klaus Weber, Jenny Frenzel, Jessica Gravening, Cami Babolik, Karen S. Steinhoff, Mike Florkowski, Maddie Elliott. For the same reason no official page was looked for (Josh Peterson on the City of Bemidji's site, Judge Mokri, the three sitting legislators' pages are already in the record), and the years of Amber Gustafson's judgeship and of Josh Peterson's council service were not looked up.

The campaign websites the candidates filed were read from the real database's sl_websites table (read-only). Each was opened before being listed. John Howie's filed site (howieforsenate.com, with and without www) answered 404 Not Found on 2026-10-02, so no website is recorded for him. Omar Fateh and Dave Baker filed none; omarfateh.com is a domain-for-sale page and is not his.

Brad Tabke's site (bradtabke.com) was found by trying the address; only its front page's first lines were read (title 'Tabke for Minnesota - Moving Shakopee Forward', with Donate, Volunteer, Yard Signs, Issues, Endorsements in its menu). The second reader should confirm it names the office or the 2026 race.

party_support (a key the loader does not read, in the shape other parts use): two party units name a candidate on their own pages without the word endorsed. Kept apart from endorsed_by; whether it is shown is John's decision.

Offices without years: Amber Gustafson's and Josh Peterson's are stated on their own campaign sites without dates; from and to are left empty rather than filled from memory. Read and left out on purpose: jobs (prosecutor, administrative law judge and judicial referee and public defender posts stated without dates, broadcast and tourism work), schools, family, church and club posts, bar association posts, and the Wellstone quotation on Mitchel Kulage's site (a quotation, not a party statement).

Privacy: the reader blanks e-mail addresses and telephone numbers before showing a page. Campaign pages shown to this session's output carried family details, schooling, employers, a church and campaign committees' mailing addresses; none of it is recorded here or anywhere else.

Verifier, 2026-10-02: all 13 addresses were opened again with the kit's User-Agent and each of the 18 findings was read on its page; every one is confirmed and nothing was removed. Two wordings were corrected: Brad Tabke's website note (the page names him, 'Shakopee's State Representative' and his committee, but not the year 2026) and Josh Peterson's office (the page says 'Currently Mayor Pro Tem' under 'Council accomplishments'; it does not use the words 'member of the council'). The two party_support items are confirmed as worded (the pages list the candidate without the word endorsed for him) and stay out of endorsed_by. The nineteen candidates the researcher never reached are still unresearched; the verifier does not research.
